Official agencies such as the China Meteorological Administration typically issue updates on steering patterns and instability that could cap or boost the daily maximum, creating the narrow distribution traders are pricing. 

Upcoming model runs and afternoon observations will likely refine whether the peak settles at 35°C or edges to 36°C before any evening convection.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent heat dome conditions over the southern Plains support efficient daytime heating for Austin on August 10, with National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance indicating mostly sunny skies, light southerly winds, and highs centered near 98–100°F. Climatological norms place the mid-August average at 98°F, while ensemble model spreads and isolated thunderstorm chances introduce modest downside risk if convection develops earlier than expected. Trader emphasis on the 96–97°F and 98–99°F bins reflects this narrow uncertainty band around near-normal maxima, with limited cool-air advection or widespread cloud cover to suppress temperatures further. Updated NWS point forecasts and afternoon model runs will clarify resolution thresholds.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
